proposals.before: On bingwu, a county magistrate named Yuwen Zhihao sent blunt counsel.
proposals.after: On bingwu, a county magistrate named Yuwen Zhishao sent blunt counsel.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宇文之邵 uses 邵 (Shao), not Hao; idiomatic Zhihao mistranscribes the given name.

proposals.before: Day bingwu: Wenzhou Qushui magistrate Yuwen Zhihao memorialized on gains and losses.
proposals.after: Day bingwu: Wenzhou Qushui magistrate Yuwen Zhishao memorialized on gains and losses.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise renders 之邵 as Zhihao; correct pinyin/transcription is Zhishao.

proposals.before: Year four, first month, day dingsi: Yingzong’s temple name was closed; the emperor took the throne.
proposals.after: Year four, first month, day dingsi: Yingzong died; the emperor took the throne.
proposals.reason: 英廟崩 means the late Yingzong died (temple metonymy), not that a temple name was closed.

proposals.before: Censor-in-chief Wang Tao and investigating censors Wu Shen and Lü Jing were punished for excessive attacks on ministers: Tao went out as Chen prefect; Shen and Jü each fined twenty jin of copper.
proposals.after: Censor-in-chief Wang Tao and investigating censors Wu Shen and Lü Jing were punished for excessive attacks on ministers: Tao went out as Chen prefect; Shen and Jing each fined twenty jin of copper.
proposals.reason: Typographical corruption Jü for Jing (呂景).

proposals.before: Third month, gengchen: Liangzha of Xia died; his court sent mourners.
proposals.after: Third month, gengchen: Liangzuo of Xia died; his court sent mourners.
proposals.reason: 諒詐 is a variant/corruption of the Xia ruler 諒祚 already named earlier; idiomatic Liangzha obscures the identity.

proposals.before: Day bingchen: Prince of Chang Hao and Prince of Le'an Jun Yun begged to leave office for mourning; not permitted.
proposals.after: Day bingchen: Prince of Chang Hao and Prince of Le'an Yun begged to leave office for mourning; not permitted.
proposals.reason: 頵 is Yun; literal 'Jun Yun' wrongly inserts an extra name syllable.

proposals.before: Winter, tenth month, day bingshen: Fu Bi was dismissed as Wuning military commissioner and Bozhou administrator.
proposals.after: Winter, tenth month, day bingshen: Fu Bi was dismissed and made Wuning military commissioner and administrator of Bozhou.
proposals.reason: 罷爲 means dismissed from his prior post and appointed as the following offices, not removed from those offices.

proposals.before: On wuxu, frontier officers Zhe Jishi and Wei Mingshan were ennobled as Zhao Huaihun.
proposals.after: On wuxu, Fan official Zhe Jishi was made prefect of Zhongzhou, and Wei Mingshan was made supply commissioner and given the name Zhao Huaishun.
proposals.reason: Chinese appoints Zhe Jishi as 忠州刺史 and only grants 嵬名山 the name 趙懷順 (Huaishun), not Huaihun; the idiomatic fuses both men under one wrong new name.

proposals.before: Day wuxu: Fan official ritual guest commissioner Zhe Jishi was made Zhong prefect; left gate guard general Wei Mingshan was made supply commissioner and given the surname Zhao and name Huaihun.
proposals.after: Day wuxu: Fan official ritual guest commissioner Zhe Jishi was made Zhong prefect; left gate guard general Wei Mingshan was made supply commissioner and given the surname Zhao and name Huaishun.
proposals.reason: 懷順 is Huaishun, not Huaihun.

proposals.before: On wuwu, Zongnu returned to the council.
proposals.after: On wuwu, Zong'e returned to the council.
proposals.reason: 宗諤 is Zong'e, not Zongnu.

proposals.before: Day wuwu: Zongnu again became co-director.
proposals.after: Day wuwu: Zong'e again became co-director.
proposals.reason: 宗諤 is Zong'e, not Zongnu.

proposals.before: On renwu, he lectured again in Yingying Hall.
proposals.after: On renwu, he heard lecture in Erying Hall.
proposals.reason: 聽講 means heard a lecture, not delivered one; 邇英閣 is Erying Hall, not Yingying Hall.

proposals.before: Day renwu: he heard lecture in Yingying Hall.
proposals.after: Day renwu: he heard lecture in Erying Hall.
proposals.reason: 邇英閣 is Erying Hall, not Yingying Hall.

decisions.reason: 宇文之邵 ends in 邵 (Shao); Zhihao wrongly reads 邵 as Hao, and Zhishao is the accurate given-name transcription.
The same unit has 宇文之邵; the literal’s Zhihao is the same mistranscription, and Zhishao matches 之邵.
英廟崩 uses temple metonymy for Yingzong’s death (崩), not the closing of a temple name; the proposed ‘died’ matches the Chinese and the idiomatic field.
呂景 is Jing; ‘Jü’ is a typographical corruption of that name already given correctly earlier in the same sentence.
Wikisource Songshi vol. 14 transmits 夏主諒詐卒 here while naming the same Xia ruler 諒祚 earlier in the juan; idiomatic Liangzuo correctly identifies him rather than inventing a distinct Liangzha.
樂安郡王頵 titles Yun as commandery prince of Le’an; ‘Jun Yun’ wrongly takes 郡 as an extra name syllable.
罷爲X means dismissal from the prior post and appointment as X; the before reading treats 武甯軍節度使、判亳州 as offices he lost rather than ones he received.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 富弼罷爲武甯軍節度使、判亳州

decisions.reason: The Chinese separately makes 折繼世忠州刺史 and makes 嵬名山供備庫使 with the granted name 趙懷順; the before fuses both men under a single wrong ennoblement as Zhao Huaihun.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 折繼世爲忠州刺史，左監門衛將軍嵬名山爲供備庫使，仍賜姓名趙懷順

decisions.reason: 懷順 is Huaishun; Huaihun misreads 順 and the proposed spelling restores the granted name.
宗諤 is Zong’e (諤); Zongnu has no support in the Chinese and the proposed form is the accurate reading.
The same unit has 宗諤; the literal’s Zongnu is the same mistranscription fixed by Zong’e.
御邇英閣聽講 means the emperor attended/heard a lecture in Erying Hall; ‘lectured again in Yingying Hall’ reverses 聽講 and misreads 邇英, inventing ‘again’.
邇英閣 is Erying Hall; Yingying Hall misreads 邇英, and the proposed hall name is accurate.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0009 shows Zhao Huaihun exists only as the bad English reading of 趙懷順; the source supports Huaishun (already claimed) and no Huaihun alias.
Accepted r0010 shows Zongnu exists only as the bad English reading of 宗諤; the source supports Zong’e and no Zongnu alias.
